text:
Jamie (CS): pinging the team — AcmeApp is seeing very odd rerank scores from /v1/rerank: negative values like -3.4 and unbounded positives 12.7. They expect normalized scores in [0,1]. Can we triage?
AcmeApp (customer): repro attached — curl and response below. This started after we moved to model=redwood-rerank-v2 yesterday. We're blocked for release.
AcmeApp (customer): ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n -d '{"model":"redwood-rerank-v2","query":"best payment gateway","candidates":["Stripe","PayPal","Braintree"]}'
```
AcmeApp (customer): response: ```json
{"model":"redwood-rerank-v2","scores":[-3.409,0.12,12.73],"candidates":["Stripe","PayPal","Braintree"]}
```
Jamie (CS): they say they used to get normalized probabilities (sum=1 or scores in 0..1). This looks like raw logits, maybe model change?
Priya (ML Eng): quick check — if the model started returning logits instead of probabilities that could explain negatives and >1. Did we change any default post-processing for rerank endpoints during the v2 rollout?
Connor (Platform): rollout notes: v2 shipped a faster scoring kernel and removed softmax in runtime for perf — we expected clients to apply normalization themselves but we didn't update docs for the hosted endpoint. Not ideal. @Priya is that consistent?
Priya (ML Eng): yes, the new kernel returns log-odds (logits) for internal eval consistency. For most internal paths we post-process; looks like a config toggle accidentally disabled runtime softmax for hosted rerank.
Sam (SRE): logs show a config flip yesterday at 2026-03-08T14:12:03Z on rerank-service that toggled "postprocess.softmax":false in stage.ops. Might be the root cause.
ops-bot: deployment 2026-03-08T14:11:59Z completed for redwood-rerank-v2 canary — changeset id c9f3d2
Jamie (CS): AcmeApp needs a quick workaround. Can we advise them on safe client-side normalization?
Priya (ML Eng): yes, recommend softmax across returned scores: softmax(x_i)=exp(x_i)/sum_j exp(x_j). For numeric stability do x' = x - max(x) before exponent. Also warn about underflow/overflow for very large logits.
AcmeApp (customer): can you give us an example snippet? We're JS node backend.
Priya (ML Eng): ```js
function softmax(scores){
  const max = Math.max(...scores);
  const exps = scores.map(s => Math.exp(s - max));
  const sum = exps.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0);
  return exps.map(e => e/sum);
}
// then map candidates to normalized probs
```
Jamie (CS): ok that'll unblock them short-term. Long term we need to either re-enable softmax in runtime or clearly document behavior and version the change. Priorities?
Connor (Platform): action items: 1) hotfix — flip postprocess.softmax back to true in hosted for stable channel (rollback canary); 2) patch release notes and API docs; 3) add explicit header or response field to indicate score_type ("logit" vs "probability"); 4) create runbook for rerank model swaps. Agree?
Priya (ML Eng): +1. Also check if Dedicated/Private customers already rely on logits - we can't silently change behavior there. Need to scope by deployment type.
Sam (SRE): I'm on the hotfix. Rolling revert to set postprocess.softmax=true for the hosted pool now. ETA ~15m. I'll monitor for errors.
ops-bot: rollback job started for config-stage 'rerank-service' by Sam — id ff12a7 — see https://ops.redwood.internal/jobs/ff12a7
Jamie (CS): I told AcmeApp the temporary client fix and that we'll follow up with timeline.
AcmeApp (customer): thanks. If you revert, will we see the older normalized scores back?
Priya (ML Eng): yes, reverting runtime postprocessing should restore probabilities. But we should also add explicit response metadata so clients don't have to guess. Example response field: "score_type":"probability" or "score_type":"logit". That prevents surprises on future model swaps.
Connor (Platform): agreed. I'll make a small API change proposal: add `score_type` (enum) + `score_normalization` (string) fields in response; feature-flagged for 2 weeks. Docs update required.
Jamie (CS): also note edgecases: if some clients previously used top-k ranking and ignored scores, they won't break. But customers that rely on absolute thresholds (score>0.5) will be affected. Add a note to customer comms.
Priya (ML Eng): follow-up investig: why did the canary config flip affect hosted but maybe not private/dedicated? We'll audit the config rev history. Could be an environment default drift.
Sam (SRE): revert completed. Monitoring: initial metrics show scores distribution returning to 0..1 range for hosted pool. No errors. Will keep watching for 30m.
ops-bot: monitor alert: rerank-score-distribution returned to expected band at 2026-03-08T14:30:12Z
Jamie (CS): sending a short postmortem to AcmeApp: root cause = inadvertent disable of hosted postprocessing (softmax) during v2 rollout; mitigation = revert + client softmax snippet + docs and API metadata change plan.
AcmeApp (customer): appreciate the quick turnaround. Please let us know when docs are updated so we can remove our client-side softmax.
Connor (Platform): I'll own the API metadata patch and docs update. Filing ticket: PLAT-8723. ETA for docs + header rollout: 5 working days.
Priya (ML Eng): I'll add unit tests to the rerank CI to assert response includes `score_type` and that hosted responses are probabilities unless explicitly configured.
Jamie (CS): final ask: Sam can you attach the job id and logs to the ticket so support can reference?
Sam (SRE): done — logs and job ff12a7 attached to PLAT-8723.
Jamie (CS): thanks everyone. Closing the escalation once docs PR lands and AcmeApp confirms. :white_check_mark:
